tools.name: review_paint_peek_latest
tools.title: Get Latest Painted Review Feedback
tools.description: Return the newest brush-painted review packet from a Studio session. After sharing a /p/<slug> link, the user can open it in the browser and paint marks over the 3D viewport to give visual feedback. Call this tool with the `slug` from that link to see the strokes — screenshot + mask + struck part names plus an optional one-line note and intent tags (e.g. "too thick", "missing", "wrong angle") describing WHAT is wrong — and act on the feedback. The slug is the capability: no OAuth required when passing `slug`; private projects require the owner to be signed in. Omit `slug` to fetch your own latest packet from your signed-in account (requires OAuth). By default returns short-lived signed Storage URLs for the screenshot + mask + meta.json plus the struck part names — small and context-friendly. Pass `paths_only: false` to also base64-inline the PNGs for clients that cannot fetch the signed URLs over HTTP.

slug.description: Project slug from open_in_studio/get_project/a /p/<slug> link. When given, returns the latest brush packet painted on that project's page — works without OAuth; the slug is the capability. Omit to use your signed-in account's latest packet.

freshness_sec.description: Maximum packet age in seconds. Default 1800 (30 min). Use a smaller value for "what did I just paint" or a larger one for "earlier today".

paths_only.description: Controls PNG delivery. Default (omitted or true): return only signed URLs + struck part names — the small, context-friendly response; fetch the bytes via the signed URLs. Set false to also base64-inline the screenshot + mask PNGs for clients that cannot fetch the URLs over HTTP (larger response).

tools.name: open_in_studio
tools.title: Open in Studio
tools.description: Save the model as a kernelCAD project AND show it: persists a project revision, returns the interactive Studio viewer (MCP Apps / ChatGPT outputTemplate), and includes a PNG preview in the SAME tool result (image content + previewUrl when available). ONE VIEWER PER PROJECT PER RESPONSE: every call renders a new viewer card. Do all validation with evaluate_script first, then call open_in_studio exactly once, after validation succeeds; reuse the returned URL, revision and preview, and never call it again after a successful result in the same response. Re-calling with unchanged code for the same project returns that revision instead of writing a new one. CONTINUE, DO NOT DUPLICATE: to change a model you already saved, pass `project: '<slug>'` from the last result (or from list_my_projects) — this adds a revision to that project. Without `project`, the save goes to the project this chat already saved, or to your project with the same title (case, punctuation and v2/rev3/(1) ignored) from the last 24 h. Views, poses, colours and options of one design are revisions of ONE project — keep the same title and slug. Pass `new_project: true` only when the user wants a separate design. A different cookbook (execute_cookbook, or open_in_studio of that cookbook's unchanged source) starts its own project; pass `project` to add a revision, or `continue_design: true` to keep revising the design this chat is already saving. The result starts with the slug to pass next time, a /p/<slug>?version= link for this revision, and that revision's title. Use this when the user wants to SEE or share the model — do NOT call get_latest_render afterwards for the happy path; the preview is already here when previewDelivered is true. Pass the full `.kcad` source as `code` (optional if you just called evaluate_script — omitting reuses that last evaluated source). Code that fails evaluate_script (for example overlapping same-material members or floating pieces) is refused; fix it first. A broken mechanism verdict alone does NOT refuse: the revision is saved, Studio shows "Mechanism broken", and the result returns mechanismSummary (statement, maxLevel, failures with the joint). Tell the user the mechanism is broken; do not call it working. Multi-body assemblies must declare connectors + mates/joints before publish — otherwise evaluate_script fails with mechanism.orphan-part (disconnected components). Use type: 'axis' + revolute mates for shafts/hinges/gears; type: 'frame' + fastened for rigid mounts; or arm.revolute/.prismatic/.ball/.fixed. Connector types are only frame|axis|planar|ball. Status fields: ok=true means the project revision was saved (projectSaved=true). meshSaved reports whether its display mesh is persisted; meshStatus=failed means meshSaved=false, but the saved project remains usable for geometry checks. Do not claim its 3D viewer is ready. previewDelivered=true means this result carries a displayable PNG — only then may you tell the user a preview was shown. meshStatus mirrors get_project (ready|building|failed|missing). Under CDN, open_in_studio waits up to ~20s (OPEN_IN_STUDIO_MESH_SYNC_BUDGET_MS) for the revision mesh before returning; heavier publishes usually land meshStatus=ready. If still meshStatus=building + meshReady=false: TRANSIENT — meshUrl is the expected CDN pin; embed retries 404s. Poll get_project({slug}) until ready (it shows no viewer) — do not re-call open_in_studio, and never treat building as permanent failure/404. ALWAYS pass `code` when you have it (avoid no_code_to_reuse); evaluate_script reuse is a fallback. Paint phases: projectSaved / meshReady / previewDelivered are set here; viewerPainted is ONLY true after widget ack (model context / widgetState) — never claim paint from this tool alone. Do NOT call get_model_mesh or get_latest_render for interactive paint. INDEPENDENT OF EXPORT/STEP: call this for shaded paint even while export is running, timed out, or returned export.deferred — mesh paint does not wait on STEP. Never block open_in_studio on a STEP download. Pass include_preview:false to skip the rasterizer (save + viewer URLs only). Trigger phrases: "open it in Studio", "let me see it", "show me the model"; also call once after you finish a build, and once per response after each meaningful revision while iterating. ORGANIC/CAR SUCCESS GATE: for final likeness claims pass likeness_profile:"automotive" (and body_bbox/wheels/still_verdicts, or a prior verify body-likeness pass for this code). If the gate fails, ok:false with DX reference.likeness.publish-blocked|gate-required — do not claim success. Omit likeness_profile for WIP previews only. Declare dimensions in the source with shape.dimension({ kind, from, to, label }) (label is a name; the measured value is appended) and they show on the model in every viewer; add ?dims=1 to a /p link to force dimensions on. MARK & FIX: a user message starting `Edit kernelCAD project <slug> (revision N): "<note>". Targets: #1 feature "<id>" ...` comes from pins the user tapped in the viewer. Feature/part ids are the script's own feature and part names (assembly part names, named shapes); points are world mm. Call get_project with that slug, change only the named features near those points, keep everything else, then open_in_studio with project set to the same slug. Hosted: lib.fromSTEP / fromSTL / fromDXF / fromSVG and referenceImage take a direct string literal or a const bound to one (computed expressions are unsupported). They accept "asset:<id>" (from request_upload), an https:// URL or a data: URI as the path.

code.description: The full .kcad source of the model to open in Studio (the script you have been editing). Optional: omit to reuse the source from your most recent evaluate_script call.

title.description: Optional human-readable title for the model (shown in Studio). Defaults to "Model from Claude".

parameters.description: Optional list of the model's editable parameters, so Studio can render parameter controls. Each item is one control derived from the .kcad params.

name.description: Parameter identifier as used in the script (e.g. "width").

defaultValue.description: Current/default value of the parameter; type matches `kind`.

kind.description: Control type Studio should render for this parameter.

unit.description: Optional unit label shown next to the control (e.g. "mm", "deg").

description.description: Optional human-readable explanation of the parameter.

project.description: Slug of the project to update (from the last open_in_studio result, a "Saved to your projects" note, list_my_projects, or a /p/<slug> link). Adds a new revision to that project instead of creating a new one, and live-updates the user's open Studio tab.

slug.description: Older name for `project`. Use `project`.

new_project.description: Pass true only when the user wants a separate, new design. Default: continue this chat's project, or your project with the same title from the last 24 h. Still wins over a matching title or cookbook.

continue_design.description: Pass true to add a revision to the design this chat is already saving, even when this call is a different cookbook or title. Ignored when `project` is set.

include_preview.description: Default true: render an iso PNG preview into this same tool result (reuses the server render cache when this source was already rendered). Set false to skip rasterization and return save/viewer URLs only.

likeness_profile.description: Hard success gate for organic/car bodies. When set, open_in_studio returns ok:false unless body-likeness is publishReady (inline body_bbox/wheels/still_verdicts, or a prior verify body-likeness pass for this exact code). Omit for WIP previews.

body_bbox.description: Body AABB { min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z] } mm — for likeness_profile gate when no session attest.

cabin_bbox.description: Optional cabin AABB for likeness gate.

wheels.description: Wheel centres + radii for likeness gate [{ center:[x,y,z], radius }].

still_verdicts.description: Agent still checklist for likeness gate [{ code, passed, finding, view? }].

attachments.description: Complementary project files referenced by relative path from the .kcad source.

anon_token.description: Anonymous owner token returned as `anonToken` by an earlier open_in_studio result. Pass it on every open_in_studio call, also in a new chat, so all your anonymous projects stay together and move to the user's account when they sign in. Omit when you have none.

intent.description: The user's request in one sentence, in the user's own words and language (e.g. 'M4 bracket for a 25 mm tube, print on Bambu A1'). Helps kernelCAD improve; leave out personal data.

ok.description: Whether the project revision was saved (same meaning as projectSaved). A failed display mesh does not make this false; inspect meshSaved and meshStatus.

meshSaved.description: Whether the revision display mesh is persisted. False while building or after meshStatus:failed.

url.description: Revision-pinned /p/<slug>?version= Studio link for the revision this call saved.

embedUrl.description: Read-only, chrome-free /embed/<slug> viewer URL — drop into an <iframe> to embed the live model in any site or widget (no login). Includes meshUrl when a revision mesh artifact is available.

meshUrl.description: Revision-matched mesh artifact URL when available — prefer this over re-executing CAD in the embed. When meshStatus is building, this is the expected CDN URL (retry until ready).

animUrl.description: CDN transforms-only animation bake URL when the script declares animationView(). ChatGPT embed Play/scrub uses this — no live session remesh.

hasAnimation.description: True when animUrl is present (animationView timeline baked at publish).

serverBuild.description: Deploy identity so connector vs server mismatch is observable.

slug.description: The project slug. Pass it back as `project` to save the next change to this project.

title.description: Title stored for this revision (not a later revision of the same project).

project_note.description: Which project was updated or created, its URL, and how to keep working on it.

version.description: Immutable Studio revision persisted by this call. Read it with get_project_revision using this slug and version.

updated.description: True when an existing project was updated; false when a new one was created.

previewDelivered.description: True when this result includes a displayable PNG (image content and/or previewUrl). Only then may the agent claim a preview was shown to the user.

previewStatus.description: included = PNG + URL; included_inline = PNG only; unavailable = save ok but no preview; skipped = include_preview:false.

previewUrl.description: HTTPS URL of the PNG preview when storage signed successfully.

meshStatus.description: ready | building | failed | missing — explicit CDN artifact state (never silently omit meshUrl under CDN mode).

meshError.description: Sanitized persist/repair error when meshStatus is failed.

meshHint.description: When meshStatus=building: transient OCCT/CDN write — poll get_project or re-open_in_studio; never imply permanent 404/failure. Present under CDN when building.

projectSaved.description: True when the project/revision was persisted. Not the same as viewerPainted.

mechanismSummary.description: Mechanism verdict of the saved code (same as evaluate_script mechanismSummary), stored with the revision for the Studio badge. maxLevel error = "Mechanism broken" (saved anyway; statement names the joint), warning = "Motion not checked", ok = "Motion checked". Absent for a static model.

viewerPainted.description: Always false on tools/call. The Studio widget sets viewerPainted:true via updateModelContext after a correlated model_displayed ack.

paintHint.description: Agent guidance: do not claim interactive paint until viewerPainted.

tools.name: get_project
tools.title: Get Project
tools.description: Use this when you need to reopen a saved project or browse what the user has saved — it fetches a kernelCAD Studio project, or lists the signed-in user's saved projects. Pass `slug` (from a /p/<slug> link or a prior listing) to fetch that project's full .kcad source and metadata — then edit and open_in_studio with the same slug so the user's open tab updates live. Private projects require their owner's OAuth connection. OMIT `slug` to list the signed-in user's saved projects (most recently updated first); that listing mode requires the OAuth connection and does NOT paint — prefer list_my_projects to find a project to continue. Read-only: this tool never shows a viewer (only open_in_studio does, once per response). Paint phases: projectSaved/meshReady reflect fetch state; viewerPainted stays false. Use open_in_studio (with code) to publish+paint — do NOT call get_model_mesh or get_latest_render for interactive paint.

slug.description: The project slug from a listing or a /p/<slug> Studio link. Omit to list the signed-in user's saved projects.
Fetch mode: the project slug.

embedUrl.description: Fetch mode: revision-pinned chrome-free /embed/<slug>?revision= viewer URL (includes meshUrl when available).

meshUrl.description: Fetch mode: revision-matched mesh artifact URL when available — FunnelViewer loads it instead of re-executing CAD. When meshStatus is building, this is the expected CDN URL (retry until ready).

meshStatus.description: Fetch mode: ready | building | failed | missing — explicit CDN artifact state (never silently omit meshUrl under CDN mode).

meshError.description: Fetch mode: sanitized repair/persist error when meshStatus is failed.

meshHint.description: Fetch mode: when meshStatus=building — transient; poll again or re-open_in_studio; never imply permanent 404.

serverBuild.description: Deploy identity (package+git SHA@boot time) so connector lag is observable.

parameters.description: Fetch mode: the model's editable parameters.

assets.description: Complementary files keyed by source-relative path.

projects.description: List mode (no slug): the user's saved projects.

projectSaved.description: Fetch mode: true when the project was loaded.

meshReady.description: Fetch mode: true only when meshStatus===ready.

viewerPainted.description: Always false on tools/call; widget sets true after correlated model_displayed.

tools.name: get_project_revision
tools.title: Get Project Revision
tools.description: Fetch the exact immutable .kcad source and parameters captured at a prior `open_in_studio` version. Use this to read-after-write verify a release: pass the returned `slug` and `version`, then hash or inspect the returned source. Public/unlisted projects use the slug as capability; private projects require the owner's OAuth connection.

slug.description: Project slug returned by open_in_studio.

version.description: Positive immutable revision version returned by open_in_studio.

ok.description: Whether the revision was found and readable.

slug.description: Project slug.

code.description: Exact .kcad source captured at this revision.

parameters.description: Exact editable parameters captured at this revision.

title.description: Title captured with this revision. Absent on revisions snapshotted before titles were stored.

tools.name: get_latest_render
tools.title: Get Latest Render
tools.description: Render a project's current model server-side and return it as an inline image so you can SEE what you built. Prefer open_in_studio for the happy path — it already includes an iso PNG preview in the same publish result when previewDelivered is true. Use this tool for a different `view`, a contact sheet (`view:"all"`), or when you only have a slug and are not publishing. Call with that `slug` to inspect whether the build looks right. CRITICAL — the image is rendered from the MODEL on the server; it does NOT reflect the user's Studio camera, zoom, or screen. NEVER ask the user to rotate, zoom, pan, move the camera, close a slider, or change their view to help you see — you cannot affect their screen and it cannot affect this render. To see a different angle, call this tool again with a different `view`. By DEFAULT (omit `view`, or `view:"all"`) it returns a CONTACT SHEET of all six canonical views in one labeled image — a 3×2 grid, top row [iso, front, right], bottom row [back, left, top] — so you can judge the model from every side regardless of its orientation (e.g. to find which side has the doors). Pass a single `view` (iso/front/back/left/right/top) for one large render of that angle. DETERMINISTIC: the same model + view always returns the same bytes — identical bytes are NOT a stale/lagging snapshot. If you changed the model, push it with open_in_studio FIRST, then re-render to see the change. The image is always current and never a blank capture. Colors and shading match Studio (same palette / base-material color). The slug is the capability: no OAuth for public/unlisted; private projects require the owner signed in. The PNG is base64-inlined as a real image block by default; pass `paths_only: true` for metadata only. No renderable geometry or a mesh failure → { ok: false, error, hint }, never a blank image. error "mesh_timeout" means the model took too long to build for a preview; the source is not wrong (it still exports) — do not rewrite it to fix the render.

slug.description: Project slug from open_in_studio/get_project/a /p/<slug> link. The slug is the capability — public/unlisted projects need no OAuth; private projects require the owner to be signed in.

view.description: View to render. Default "all" = a labeled contact sheet of every canonical angle (iso/front/back/left/right/top) — best for judging the whole model. Pass a single view name for one large render of that angle.

paths_only.description: Controls PNG delivery. Default false: base64-inline the rendered PNG so clients that cannot fetch a URL over HTTP (e.g. a sandboxed agent) can still see it. Set true to return only metadata (smaller response).

image_b64.description: Base64-encoded PNG bytes, present when inlined (paths_only=false) and under the size cap.

truncated.description: Set when inline was requested but the PNG exceeded the size cap.

view.description: The view that was rendered (when ok).

width.description: Rendered image edge in px (when ok).

height.description: Rendered image edge in px (when ok).

error.description: Error code when ok is false (e.g. "empty_geometry", "mesh_failed", "mesh_timeout").

hint.description: Next-action hint when ok is false.

tools.name: get_model_mesh
tools.title: Get Model Mesh
tools.description: Return the raw per-feature triangle mesh (positions/indices/normals) of a project's current model, by slug. For the in-chat 3D viewer widget to render geometry; delivered over the MCP Apps bridge. The slug is the capability: public/unlisted need no OAuth; private requires the owner signed in.

slug.description: Project slug from open_in_studio/get_project.

tools.name: request_upload
tools.title: Request File Upload
tools.description: Use this when the user has a photo, PDF drawing, STEP, STL, DXF, SVG or 3MF file on their device and you need it in a kernelCAD tool (trace_from_image, drawing_to_cad, mesh_to_features, inspect of:"step", or lib.fromSTEP / fromSTL / fromDXF / fromSVG / referenceImage in a script). Do not ask the user to paste the file as text or base64, and do not type coordinates from an image by hand. Returns a one-time `uploadUrl` (valid 30 minutes) and an `asset` reference. Give the user the link; after they say the upload is done, pass the `asset` value ("asset:<id>") as the file argument, for example trace_from_image({ imageUrl: "asset:<id>" }) or lib.fromSTEP("asset:<id>"). If the file is already at a public https:// URL, pass that URL instead. On clients that support MCP URL elicitation the upload page opens for the user directly and the call returns once the file is stored (status "uploaded"); then use the asset right away without asking the user anything.

purpose.description: Optional short note shown on the upload page, e.g. "the photo of the worn bracket".

tools.name: lookup_authoring_skill
tools.title: Look Up Authoring Skill
tools.description:
Return the kernelcad-authoring skill — conventions for writing .kcad.ts scripts (API surface, parameters, evaluation contract, common pitfalls) — in sections.

Call with NO arguments first: you get the quick-start (units, axes, the return rule, the rules that prevent most failures, the intent → API routing table, the "Before you finish" checklist) and an index of every section with a one-line summary (under 16k chars). Then pull what you need: `{ section: "<id>" }` returns one section (e.g. "top-level-functions", "materials", "dfm-gates-print-readiness"); `{ query: "fillet after subtract" }` returns the best-matching sections. `{ section: "all" }` returns the full ~140k-char skill (SKILL.md plus its reference files) — only if your client accepts large responses.

Clients that list resources can also read `kernelcad://skills/authoring` (the SKILL.md core).

OUTPUT: { uri, mimeType, mode, text, sections? } — `mode` is index | section | search | all | not-found.

section.description: Section id from the index (e.g. 'top-level-functions'), or 'all' for the full skill.

topic.description: Alias of section; also accepts a loose title such as 'materials' or 'cli commands'.

query.description: Keywords to search section titles and bodies (e.g. "sweep along helix").

tools.name: mesh_summary
tools.title: Summarize Mesh Geometry
tools.description:
Mesh a kernelCAD .kcad.ts source server-side and return a COMPACT geometry summary — overall bounds plus, per feature, its id, kind, triangle count, and bounding box.

Use this to INSPECT a model's geometry without a viewer: confirm a part is the size/shape you expect, see how many triangles each feature contributes, or check that every feature produced geometry. This runs the full server-side OCCT pipeline (the same one the Studio renderer uses), so it evaluates modern sources (assembly, path, .material, …) that the legacy client worker cannot.

INPUT: `source` (required) the .kcad.ts script text; `fileName` (optional) a label for diagnostics; `params` (optional) a map of parameter-name → number overrides applied before meshing (stateless slider recompute).

OUTPUT: { ok, bounds, featureCount, features: [{ id, kind, triangleCount, bbox: { min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z] } }], failedFeatureIds, diagnostics }. `ok` is true when every feature meshed; `failedFeatureIds` lists features that failed to compile (and `ok` is then false). Raw vertex/index/normal arrays are NEVER returned — this is a summary only. To SEE the rendered model, call open_in_studio (includes PNG preview + viewer); use get_latest_render only for alternate views.

fileName.description: Optional file-name label used in diagnostics (does not affect geometry).

params.description: Optional map of parameter-name → numeric value, applied as overrides before meshing (stateless slider recompute).

tools.name: evaluate_script
tools.title: Evaluate CAD Script
tools.description: Use this when you need to run a script and check it compiles. Full local builds return viewerUrl: a live Studio link reused and updated on later full builds in the same MCP process. Hosted builds return viewerMode: hosted and viewerHint pointing to open_in_studio; they do not start a loopback viewer. Full evaluations return step evidence: build validity, volume and before/after local PNG paths in one shared iso frame. Snapshots require PW_CDP_URL for an existing browser; unavailable captures report an explicit error. Run a kernelCAD .kcad.ts script and report pass/fail + feature count + diagnostics + sceneSummary (BREP validity, volume in mm³, face count, bounding size in mm). When the scene is assembly-built (assembly().part(...) → .model()/.solvedModel()), also returns a parts summary { count, names } AND runs the mechanism-truth gate by default: the `mechanism` field reports real/broken/unverified and a broken mechanism (disconnected components / mechanism.orphan-part, self-collision, fastened drift, dof-mismatch) makes ok:false with the failures in diagnostics, as does a mate connector more than 6 mm outside its part bounding box (assembly.mechanical.connector-not-in-solid, the same error review_cad reports) — a mechanism (any mate or joint) needs every part linked by connectors + mates/joints (axis+revolute for shafts/hinges/gears; frame+fastened for rigid; or arm.revolute/.prismatic/.ball/.fixed). A plain multi-part assembly with no mates (base + lid, print layout) is independent bodies and passes. Pass { skipMechanismCheck: true } to opt out (e.g. a deliberately free part next to a mechanism). An animation or drive on a fastened joint (mechanism.motion-on-fixed-joint) is broken: animate a revolute/prismatic mate pose. For a model with moving joints or motion intent, `mechanismSummary.statement` is one plain line: "Motion checked: ..." names what ran; "Motion not checked: ..." is NOT a pass — never call that mechanism working. Every union() is checked too (no opt-out): union.disconnected (the union is several separate solids — a floating operand) and union.member-overlap (two operands that each carry their own .finish()/.material(), the same one, share > 1 mm³ — cut members to fit, e.g. a cross tube between rails is span minus two rail widths) make ok:false. Pass either { file: "<path>" } or { code: "<inline source>" }. Set { dryRun: true } for fast validation while iterating: transpile + capture + capture-light checks without building solids, DFM gates, or meshing — milliseconds instead of seconds (100x+ on boolean/fillet-heavy scripts). A dry run catches script throws, capture-time API misuse, and assembly validity-gate failures, but NOT lowering failures or dfmSpec diagnostics; it leaves the active session untouched, so finish with a full (non-dry) evaluate_script before using session-dependent tools. To show a measurement in the 3D viewer (e.g. hole spacing), declare it in the script with shape.dimension({ kind: "linear", from, to, label }); a full evaluate lists them as dimensions: [{ text, kind, source }], and a shared /p link with ?dims=1 forces them on. Hosted: lib.fromSTEP / fromSTL / fromDXF / fromSVG and referenceImage take a direct string literal or a const bound to one (computed expressions are unsupported). They accept "asset:<id>" (from request_upload), an https:// URL or a data: URI as the path.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script file. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

dryRun.description: Fast validation only: skip solid build, DFM gates, and meshing. Does not set or clear the active session.

kernel.description: Solid-modeling kernel. Default 'occt' (OpenCascade); opt-in 'smlib' uses guarded candidates with explicit OCCT fallback diagnostics.

skipMechanismCheck.description: Opt out of the default mechanism-truth gate. By default a full evaluation of an assembly-built scene runs checkMechanismTruth and returns a `mechanism` verdict (real/broken/unverified); a broken mechanism makes ok:false. Set true to skip the sweep entirely (no `mechanism` field, no cost). Ignored for dryRun and non-assembly scripts.

intent.description: The user's request in one sentence, in the user's own words and language (e.g. 'M4 bracket for a 25 mm tube, print on Bambu A1'). Helps kernelCAD improve; leave out personal data.

tools.name: diff_scripts
tools.title: Diff CAD Scripts
tools.description: Use this when you need to see exactly what changed between two script versions. Structured geometric delta between two versions of a kernelCAD script — a baseline ({ baseFile } or { baseCode }) and a revision ({ file } or { code }). Returns agent-readable JSON: per-part added/removed/renamed/changed (volume mm³ + exact bbox deltas, numbers matching inspect({ of: 'part-stats' })), total interference-volume delta with per-pair detail, mate-graph changes (added/removed/changed mates incl. type, connectors, pose, limits), and param changes (value/min/max). Single-shape scripts diff as one "(root)" pseudo-part; a `return [a, b]` multi-body script diffs per body as "body[0]", "body[1]". An error that still leaves geometry (e.g. a skipped fillet) is listed under base/revised.errors beside the diff. Use after editing a script to verify exactly what changed physically before re-rendering. On a hosted server pass both versions inline: { baseCode: 'return box(10, 10, 10);', code: 'return box(10, 10, 12);' } (base_code/old_code/before and revised_code/new_code/after are accepted as aliases). Read-only — never touches the active session.

baseFile.description: Baseline (before) script — path to a .kcad.ts file. Local servers only. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

baseCode.description: Baseline (before) script — inline source. One of baseFile / baseCode is required.

file.description: Revised (after) script — path to a .kcad.ts file. Local servers only. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

code.description: Revised (after) script — inline source. One of file / code is required.

tools.name: inspect
tools.title: Inspect Model
tools.description:
Use this when you need to read facts about a model. One reader, selected by `of`:
- 'assembly' — physical assembly inventory (parts, bboxes, connectors, mates, disconnected solids).
- 'robot' — URDF/SDFormat export preview (links, joints, planning groups, end-effectors, issues).
- 'step' — inspect an imported STEP file: solid tree, exact bbox/volume, cylindrical holes (breached bores flagged partial; holeDetection: 'exact' | 'heuristic').
- 'shape' — volume / surfaceArea / bbox for one feature ({ feature_id? }).
- 'mass' — mass, centre of mass, centroidal inertia tensor (inertia6 + 3x3 inertiaMatrix), principalMoments/principalAxes, symmetry flags, and optionally the radius of gyration about an arbitrary axis ({ feature_id?, density?, gyration_axis? }); density in kg/m^3, defaults to 1000 (water).
- 'features' — features captured by the script (kind, id, params, transforms, suppression).
- 'assemblies' — assembly intent (assemblies, parts, connectors, joints).
- 'topology' — canonical face names + edge count for a feature ({ feature_id? }).
- 'edges' — edges of a shape with optional EdgeQuery ({ feature_id?, query? }); returns @kc[...] refs.
- 'face-edges' — boundary edges of a named canonical face ({ feature_id?, face_name }).
- 'faces' — faces of a shape with optional FaceQuery ({ feature_id?, query? }); returns @kc[...] refs.
- 'face-labels' — user-applied labels visible in the script.
- 'mates' — mates captured by the script.
- 'constraints' — sketch constraints captured by the script.
- 'part-stats' — bundled parts-catalog statistics.
- 'bend-table' — sheet-metal bend table for a flattened pattern.
- 'params' — declared model parameters.
- 'part-categories' — top-level part-catalog categories available in the bundled (and configured remote) catalog.
- 'part-families' — part families within a category ({ category? }); count + exemplar ids per family.
- 'bom' — bill of materials ({ assembly? }): one row per distinct part (grouped by geometry/catalog identity, not name) with real instance quantity, kind ('fabricated'|'purchased'), material, density, per-unit and total mass, bbox, a fabrication process hint, catalog provenance for purchased parts, and totals; `bom.*` diagnostics flag rows with no density source or missing catalog vendor info instead of guessing.
- 'section' — numeric cross-section probe of a shape: area, perimeter, loop/hole counts, 2D bbox at a plane ({ feature_id?, plane | at+axis, stack?: { from, to, count, axis? } }). `stack` scans evenly spaced slices and returns `minAreaIndex`/`minAreaPosition` — use it to find the neck/thinnest cross-section along an axis.
- 'continuity' — G0/G1/G2 classification of shared edges ({ feature_id?, edges? }); position gap, normal jump, curvature difference, worst-sample XYZ.
- 'curvature' — per-face Gaussian and mean curvature min/max/mean, inflections, spikes ({ feature_id?, faces?, spike_factor? }).
- 'multi-material' — explicit material leaves shadowed by later attributed boolean descendants, with assembly-part rewrite templates; analyzes capture records and does not change mesh attribution.
All params except `of` are subject-specific and forwarded verbatim. Most subjects accept { file | code }. Hosted: give the file as an https:// URL, a data: URI (base64, max 25 MB) or "asset:<id>" from request_upload (when the file is on the user's device).

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script file. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project. Hosted server: pass an https:// URL, a data: URI, or "asset:<id>" from request_upload — not a path on your machine.

assembly.description: of:'assembly'|'robot'|'bom' — assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

feature_id.description: of:'shape'|'mass'|'topology'|'edges'|'faces'|'face-edges'|'face-labels' — FeatureId; defaults to the last returned shape.

density.description: of:'mass' — material density in kg/m^3 (steel 7850, aluminium 2700, ABS 1050). Defaults to 1000 (water); the response echoes the value used and flags when it was defaulted.

gyration_axis.description: of:'mass' — optional axis in shape-local mm to report the radius of gyration about. Omit for centroidal quantities only; the result is density-independent and returned in mm.

origin.description: A point on the axis, shape-local mm.

direction.description: Axis direction; normalised internally, so it need not be a unit vector.

face_name.description: of:'face-edges' — canonical face name (required for that subject).

category.description: of:'part-families' — optional top-level category to filter families by.

plane.description: of:'section' — section plane. Either a cardinal name string 'xy'|'xz'|'yz', { plane: 'xy'|'xz'|'yz', offset? }, or { origin: [x,y,z], normal: [nx,ny,nz] }. Omit to use `at`+`axis`.

stack.description: of:'section' — dense scan: `count` slices evenly spaced from `from` to `to` along `axis`; response reports minAreaIndex/minAreaPosition.

edges.description: of:'continuity' — optional EdgeQuery or @kc[...] ref(s) limiting which shared edges are sampled.

faces.description: of:'curvature' — optional FaceQuery or @kc[...] ref(s) limiting which faces are sampled.

spike_factor.description: of:'curvature' — spike sensitivity as a multiple of the face's Gaussian stddev (default 6).

tools.name: verify
tools.title: Verify Design
tools.description:
Use this when you need to check a design against a rule set. One verifier, selected by `check`:
- 'assembly' — static assembly review ({ file | code }, or the session evaluate_script left): mate validator, default-pose interference, joint topology, mechanical plausibility. ok:false with `blocking[]` exactly when review_cad's blocking rules fire on these findings; review_cad also sweeps joint ranges and runs physics.
- 'urdf' — structural validity of a .urdf file ({ urdf_path }).
- 'dfm' — print-readiness gates declared by dfmSpec() ({ file | code }).
- 'dfm-preflight' — sheet-metal flat pattern vs a job-shop's ordering rules ({ vendor, material, thicknessIn|thicknessMm, ... }). Returns the vendor's catalog source pages as `sources`; when `disclosure` is present, show it with those links.
- 'assembly-path' — continuous straight-line removal of each assembly part along ±X/±Y/±Z and optional world-space directions. Returns valid directions and blocking parts; disassemblyOrder runs a deterministic greedy removal pass. Watertight mesh approximation, conservative contact, no rotation/mate/hardware certification.
- 'swept-collision' — sweep declared joint range(s) and report colliding poses.
- 'reachable' — inverse-kinematics reachability for an end-effector ({ tip_link, target_position, ... }).
- 'geometry-quality' — one solid body's BREP tiny faces and short edges (ids, locations, mm²/mm), plus sampled mirror symmetry about centroid XY/YZ/XZ and principal inertia planes ({ file | code, feature_id?, tiny_face_area_mm2?, tiny_face_relative?, short_edge_length_mm?, symmetry_tolerance_mm?, mesh_deflection_mm?, asserted_plane?: { origin, normal } }). Relative area is a fraction of total surface area; thresholds are ORed. Candidate planes are discovery; only an asserted plane gates symmetry. Approximate sampled tessellation, not exact BREP proof.
- 'fastener-installation' — measured explicit catalog-screw installation stations on lowered assembly BREP ({ file | code, fasteners:[{ part, against, engagementPart?, minEngagementMm?, maxProtrusionMm? }], toleranceMm?, angleToleranceDeg? }). Reports annular bearing gap, bore axis/diameter/overlap and receiver geometric engagement/protrusion. Unknown or zero coverage cannot pass. Simplified threads do not certify torque, preload or strength.
- 'mounting-holes' — fastened mates: hole pairs one screw can use (equal, or clearance over a tap drill / hole({ thread }) of the same metric size; hole-free faces are a rigid bond) and fastener holes meeting at the contact face are coaxial. Sides it cannot resolve are info, never mismatches.
- 'load-capacity' — will it hold? Closed-form Euler-Bernoulli beam check ({ loads, materials, ... }), or mode:'fea' to solve the script's feaStudy (quadratic-tet FEA, CalculiX) — both return { ok, safetyFactor, elements[{ partName, stressPa, yieldPa, safetyFactor }], failures[], diagnostics }; fea adds the threshold, the stress regions as @kc[...] faces with their location, and fea { peakStressPa, maxDisplacementMm, meshTrusted, peakAtSupportPa, refinement }; it refines the mesh automatically until the stress is trusted (refine: false for one solve).
- 'static-hold' — gravitational holding torque/force at a sampled pose grid vs each actuated joint's declared actuator capacity ({ joint?, pose?, gravity?, min_torque_margin_pct?, range_samples? }).
- 'motion-load' — loads on each driven joint (mechanicalJoint on a revolute mate) while the model moves: gravity, inertia from the animationView tracks (finite differences), optional external forces. Mass and inertia come from the solids and density/material, or a part's massKg. Returns per joint peak torque vs the mechanicalJoint torqueNm (margin; < 1x error, < 2x warning), axial / radial force and bending moment on the actuator shaft (checked only against radialLimitN / axialLimitN; without them 'no rating, not checked'), the radial load on each of up to two coaxial supports (each at its station on the shaft: the actuator at the joint origin, else the support's connector on the axis, else the middle of its material nearest the shaft; an ambiguous station is a mechanism.load.not-resolved warning, not a number), the worst pose and a torque-vs-time series ({ file | code, motion_mode?: 'tracks'|'range', sample_ms?, range_samples?, quasi_static?, gravity?, motion_loads?: [{ part, point, force, fromMs?, toMs? }], supports?: { joint: [parts] }, series_points? }). Pass supports to compare with and without a bushing. Rigid bodies, tree mate graphs, no friction.
- 'body-likeness' — publish gate for organic/car bodies: cheap AABB↔wheel checks plus required agent still verdicts (side-body-over-wheels, side-cabin-aft, rear-haunch, ortho-proportions-vs-reference). Pass { body_bbox | code/file+body_feature_id, wheels?, cabin_bbox?, still_verdicts?, require_stills? }. Full CV silhouette matching is NOT implemented — agents must inspect ortho PNGs/Studio and supply still_verdicts before claiming success.
- 'edge-radius' — general edge-break specification on final BREP ({ file | code, min_radius_mm?, max_radius_mm?, require_edge_break?: 'external'|'internal'|'all', feature_id?, assembly?, parts?, edges?, faces? }). Reports sharp convex/concave edges, analytic cylindrical/toroidal fillet radii and spherical junctions, and heuristic planar chamfer strips. Radius bounds apply only to fillets; selectors/points are part-local. Unknown/empty coverage cannot pass.
All params except `check` are check-specific and forwarded verbatim; each check fails closed on its own missing required params.

assembly.description: Assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

max_radius_mm.description: check:'edge-radius' — maximum fillet radius in mm; must be >= min_radius_mm.

require_edge_break.description: check:'edge-radius' — prohibit sharp convex/external, concave/internal, or all edges.

edges.description: check:'edge-radius' — EdgeQuery or @kc[...] edge ref(s); intersected with faces. Query near sorts, it does not filter.

faces.description: check:'edge-radius' — FaceQuery or @kc[...] face ref(s); includes incident edges and fillets on selected faces.

fasteners.description: check:'fastener-installation' — explicit named stations; empty means no coverage.

minEngagementMm.description: Declared geometric axial overlap minimum; no thread-strength claim.

angleToleranceDeg.description: check:'fastener-installation' — axis tilt tolerance, default 1 degree.

dxf.description: check:'dfm-preflight' — path to a DXF file.

vendor.description: check:'dfm-preflight' — vendor SKU (required for that check).

material.description: check:'dfm-preflight' — material SKU (required for that check).

directions.description: check:'assembly-path' — additional nonzero world-space removal vectors; normalized and deduplicated.

joint.description: check:'swept-collision' — joint to sweep; omit to sweep every declared joint. check:'static-hold' — joint to evaluate; omit to evaluate every joint with a declared actuator.

tip_link.description: check:'reachable' — end-effector part name (required for that check).

target_position.description: check:'reachable' — target [x, y, z] mm (world frame).

target_orientation.description: check:'reachable' — target XYZ Euler angles in radians.

prefer_solver.description: check:'reachable' — force the IK path ('auto' default).

seed.description: check:'reachable' — numeric IK seed pose (joint name -> deg/mm).

loads.description: check:'load-capacity' — partName -> { force?: [Fx,Fy,Fz] N, torque?: [Tx,Ty,Tz] N*m }.

mode.description: check:'load-capacity' — 'beam' (default), 'stub', or 'fea' (solve the script's feaStudy: CalculiX + gmsh when installed, else the in-process voxel estimate).

safety_factor_threshold.description: check:'load-capacity' — pass/fail safety-factor floor (default 1.5; mode 'fea': the study's minSafetyFactor when declared).

study.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — feaStudy name (default: the last declared one).

mesh_size.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — element size override, mm.

heatmaps.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — also render stress heatmap PNGs (default false).

refine.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — one automatic finer pass (0.75x element size) when the stress is untrusted, inside the element budget (default true); false solves once at the study's meshSize.

tools.name: why_did_this_fail
tools.title: Explain Failure
tools.description: Use this when you need to trace why a feature failed. Walk the upstream chain of a failing feature. Returns the diagnostics of the requested feature plus the diagnostics of every upstream feature in topological order (the requested feature is the last entry). Per-code hints are inline on every diagnostic — call lookup_diagnostics for the full catalogue. Pass { file?, code?, feature_id? }.
