tools.name: resolve_assumptions
tools.title: Resolve Image Assumptions
tools.description: Use this when you need to confirm or override the open facts in an assumption ledger from trace_from_image (missing scale, inferred/assumed values) before committing geometry built from a reference photo. Reads the persisted `<model>.ledger.json` at `ledgerPath`, applies each resolution — `{ id, confirm: true }` to accept a fact as-is, or `{ id, value }` to override it — rewrites the ledger file, and returns the updated ledger plus `paramOverrides` (factId -> value) to feed straight into `set_param`. Pair with the `kernelcad-from-reference` skill.

ledgerPath.description: Path to the `<model>.ledger.json` file persisted alongside the traced source.

resolutions.description: One resolution per ledger fact id to act on.

value.description: Overrides the fact's value; marks it `overridden`.

confirm.description: Accepts the fact as-is; marks it `confirmed`.

tools.name: run_fea
tools.title: Run Structural FEA
tools.description:
Use this when you need to know whether a part will hold a load. Runs a linear-static structural study and returns evidence — peak von Mises stress (MPa), peak displacement (mm), the minimum safety factor against the material yield (taken away from the clamp-singular edges of the fixed faces; the raw clamp-edge peak is reported separately as peakAtSupportMPa), per-region hot spots named by @kc[...] face ref, mesh trust flags, an equilibrium residual, and (CalculiX only) stress-heatmap PNG paths.
The study is EITHER declared in the script with `shape.feaStudy({ material, fixed, loads, meshSize?, minSafetyFactor? })` OR passed on the call against the shape the script returns: { code: 'return box(100, 20, 10);', material: 'aluminum-6061', fixed: { atX: 0 }, loads: [{ faces: { atX: 100 }, force: [0, 0, -200] }] }. Faces are a FaceQuery ({ atX | atY | atZ, byNormal: 'Z', near: [x,y,z], ... }), a face label ('top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right', 'front', 'back'; it must name ONE face — after a boolean 'top' can be several, which is an error listing them) or an @kc[...] ref. Force is the TOTAL [Fx, Fy, Fz] in N on those faces (a scalar force + direction is accepted). Materials: mild-steel, aluminum-6061, pla, petg, abs, nylon (aliases steel, aluminum), or { E, nu, yield } in MPa.
Solver (`solver`, default 'auto'): CalculiX + gmsh quadratic tets when that toolchain is installed; otherwise the built-in in-process voxel solver (8-node incompatible-mode bricks), which needs nothing installed and is marked summary.solver 'in-process-voxel' with trust.meshTrusted false — an estimate (accurate for prismatic bending, approximate at curved faces and notches), never a verified pass. solver: 'calculix' fails up front with fea.solver.unavailable and the install command when the toolchain is absent.
Also: `study` (a declared study name; default the last), `output_dir` (keeps the deck / summary JSON), `mesh_size` (mm, overrides the study for this run), `heatmaps: false` for a numbers-only run. CalculiX mesh refinement is automatic: when the stress is untrusted only because the solver's error estimate is high, it re-solves once at 0.75x the element size (inside the element budget), with summary.refinement listing each pass. `refine: false` solves once.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script declaring at least one feaStudy. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

code.description: Inline kernelCAD script source (mutually exclusive with file).

study.description: Name of the declared study to run; defaults to the last declared one.

material.description: Inline study: material grade name (e.g. 'aluminum-6061') or { E, nu, yield } in MPa.

fixed.description: Inline study: faces held fixed — a FaceQuery like { atX: 0 }, a face label like 'bottom', or an @kc[...] ref.

loads.description: Inline study: loads, each { faces, force: [Fx, Fy, Fz] } — total force in N on those faces.

min_safety_factor.description: Inline study: required minimum safety factor; below it the call fails with fea.safety-factor.below-min.

solver.description: 'auto' (default): CalculiX when installed, else in-process. 'calculix': require it. 'in-process': always the built-in voxel solver.

output_dir.description: Directory for the solver deck, results, summary JSON and heatmap PNGs.

mesh_size.description: Target element size in mm, overriding the study for this run.

refine.description: One automatic finer pass (0.75x element size) when the stress is untrusted, inside the element budget (default true). false: one solve at mesh_size.

tools.name: fea_summary
tools.title: Get FEA Summary
tools.description: Use this when you need a structural check's context without paying for a solve. Read-only: returns the stored summary of a previous run_fea (pass the same `output_dir`), whether the CalculiX + gmsh toolchain is available on this machine (with the install command when it is not; run_fea then uses its in-process voxel solver — toolchain.default_solver says which), and the FEA material table with real E / Poisson / yield numbers so a grade is chosen against data rather than from memory. Never meshes, solves, or writes.

output_dir.description: Directory a previous run_fea wrote to; omit for toolchain status + material table only.

tools.name: send_to_printer
tools.title: Send G-code to Printer
tools.description: Use this when you need to upload a .gcode file (e.g. written by export with target: "model", format: "gcode") to a real network printer and, by default, start the print. protocol: 'octoprint' (POST /api/files/local with an X-Api-Key), 'moonraker' (Klipper's POST /server/files/upload), or 'bambu-lan' (Bambu Lab LAN-mode: FTPS implicit-TLS upload on port 990 as user 'bblp' with the printer's LAN access code, then an MQTT print-start command on port 8883 — requires access_code and, unless start_print is false, serial). bambu-lan uploads a .gcode.3mf print project (the printer prints 3MF projects, not bare G-code): the G-code goes in as Metadata/plate_1.gcode, inside the model 3MF from export format '3mf' when model_3mf_path is given (use options { arrange: 'plate', slicer: 'bambu' } so the printer shows the same named, coloured parts), else inside a minimal 3MF shell; the file name always ends in .3mf ('part.gcode' -> 'part.gcode.3mf'). Optional printer (a bundled profile id, the same ids as the export 3mf/gcode options.printer) is checked against protocol before anything is read or sent: an unknown id is refused with the list of valid ids, 'bambu-lan' needs a Bambu Lab profile and a Bambu Lab profile needs 'bambu-lan'. Pass { dry_run: true } to validate connectivity/authentication only, without uploading or starting a print. Never logs or echoes api_key/access_code.

gcode_path.description: Path to the .gcode file on disk.

access_code.description: Bambu LAN-mode access code (printer settings -> LAN Only Mode).

serial.description: Bambu printer serial number (required to start a print unless start_print is false).

model_3mf_path.description: bambu-lan only: model .3mf from export format '3mf' to package the G-code into (the uploaded .gcode.3mf).

printer.description: Printer profile id; checked against protocol before upload. List them with 'kernelcad print printers'.

start_print.description: Start the print immediately after upload (default: true).

dry_run.description: Validate connectivity/auth only; never uploads or starts a print.

tools.name: repair_script
tools.title: Repair CAD Script
tools.description: Use this when evaluate_script reported an error and you want the fix applied rather than described. Takes the candidates why_did_this_fail derives for a diagnostic, applies them one at a time, re-evaluates after each, and keeps the first that clears the diagnostic without introducing new errors. Never edits outside the repair region (failing feature statement + its input statements + the param() lines it reads) — an out-of-region patch is refused with tool.repair.out-of-region. Returns the repaired source in `new_code` (the caller persists it), a unified `diff`, and before/after health maps. Pass { file? | code?, diagnostic?: '<id>'|'first-error', strategy?: 'apply-first'|'try-all'|'dry-run', max_attempts?: number }.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script file. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

diagnostic.description: Diagnostic id from why_did_this_fail's `targetDiagnosticId` / `candidates[].diagnosticId`, or 'first-error' (default) for the first error-severity diagnostic.

strategy.description: 'try-all' (default) walks candidates until one clears the diagnostic; 'apply-first' applies only the top candidate and reports what it did; 'dry-run' previews every candidate patch without evaluating.

max_attempts.description: Upper bound on candidates attempted (default 3). Ignored by apply-first and dry-run.

intent.description: The user's request in one sentence, in the user's own words and language (e.g. 'M4 bracket for a 25 mm tube, print on Bambu A1'). Helps kernelCAD improve; leave out personal data.

tools.name: sweep_tolerance
tools.title: Sweep Tolerance Range
tools.description: Use this when you need to check whether a mechanism stays buildable across a tolerance/dimension range, not just at one nominal value. Declares one or more param() names with a { values: [...] } list or a { min, max, steps } range, re-evaluates the script once per cartesian-product combination (capped at 64 combos — exceeding it truncates to the first 64 and emits kinematic.sweep-tolerance.combo-cap-exceeded), and runs the standard gates on each combo: interference, mounting-hole diameter agreement, and joint-axis binding (all three, default on); reachability only when gates.reachable names a tip_link + target. Returns the pass/fail envelope table (one row per combo) plus firstFailure per gate — the fastest way to find the first param value at which a design breaks.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script file. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

assembly.description: Assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

params.description: param() name -> { values: [number|string, ...] } or { min, max, steps }.

gates.description: Which standard gates to run per combo.

reachable.description: Runs the reachability gate when set.

tools.name: diff_geometry
tools.title: Diff Model Geometry
tools.description: Use this when you need to know WHAT MATERIAL changed between two versions of a model, not just how much. The deeper sibling of diff_scripts: a volume delta alone is ambiguous (a boss that grew and a pocket that deepened report the same magnitude, and a part that only moved reports zero), so this tool answers it with geometry instead of pixels. Baseline is { baseFile } or { baseCode }; the revised side is either another script ({ file } or { code }) or the SAME script re-lowered with { params } overrides — a bag of declared param() name -> new value, which is the one-script form a parameter sweep actually asks for. Bodies pair by name and fall back to declaration-order positional pairing; anything left over is listed in `unmatched` and raises diff.body.unmatched. Per matched body it returns addedMm3 = volume(revised - base), removedMm3 = volume(base - revised), commonMm3 = volume of the overlap from boolean intersection, exact bbox with min/max/extent deltas, face / edge / hole count deltas (hole counts reuse the cylindrical-hole detector), maxDeviationMm (two-sided discrete Hausdorff distance between the two surfaces), and a `verdict` — identical | moved | resized | topology-changed, precedence topology-changed > resized > moved > identical. Branch on the verdict; cite the numbers. Optional { render: true } also writes an overlay PNG (added green, removed red, unchanged material as a translucent ghost; the scene is a re-runnable .kcad.ts over lossless BREP sidecars) through the render_preview pipeline and fails open (the numeric diff is still returned) when that pipeline is unavailable. Read-only — never touches the active session.

baseFile.description: Baseline script — path to a .kcad.ts file. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

file.description: Revised script — path to a .kcad.ts file. Mutually exclusive with params. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project.

code.description: Revised script — inline source. Mutually exclusive with params.

params.description: Param-override mode: re-lower the BASELINE with these declared param() values changed (e.g. { plateThickness: 8 }). Mutually exclusive with file/code. A name the baseline does not declare fails with the declared-param list in the message.

render.description: Also render an overlay PNG — added material green, removed material red — via the render_preview pipeline. Off by default; the numeric table is the agent-facing evidence.

out_dir.description: Directory for the overlay PNG, its STL inputs, and the generated overlay script. Default: a temp dir.

tools.name: drawing_to_cad
tools.title: Convert Drawing to CAD
tools.description: Use this when the reference for a part is a 2D engineering drawing PDF (orthographic views with dimensions), not a photo. Deterministic, no vision model: reads the vector linework (stroke width, dash) and positioned text; classifies visible / hidden / center / dimension / extension lines; reads the title block scale, units and projection symbol; identifies front / top / side views by projection alignment (third- or first-angle); ties dimension text to its lines (⌀, R, 4×, ±, THRU, depth). Dimension values win over measured lengths. Rebuilds the part as the view silhouette extruded by the depth an orthogonal view shows, or a turned part revolved from its half-silhouette, plus holes from ⌀ circles with THRU or hidden-line depth. Returns `script` — a `.kcad.ts` with role-named params (width, thickness, holeDia, hole1X, dia1, step1Length …) — and `ledger`, an assumption ledger where stated dimensions are `visible`, symmetry-derived positions `inferred`, defaults `assumed` and an unstated depth `missing`; a dimension that disagrees with the linework keeps its value and records the disagreement as an open fact. With verify (default) the script is evaluated, re-projected through the svg-drawing view stage and compared: `fidelity.verdict` is match | partial | mismatch | failed with per-axis extents, hole diameters and per-view silhouette IoU. Pass `out` to write the script and its `<stem>.ledger.json` (resolve open facts with resolve_assumptions, then set_param). A scanned (raster-only) page fails with reference.drawing.raster-only — use trace_from_image for those. Hosted: give the file as an https:// URL, a data: URI (base64, max 25 MB) or "asset:<id>" from request_upload (when the file is on the user's device).

path.description: Path to the drawing PDF on the machine running kernelCAD. Hosted server: pass an https:// URL, a data: URI, or "asset:<id>" from request_upload — not a path on your machine.

pdfBase64.description: The PDF inline, base64-encoded. Use this instead of `path` against a hosted kernelCAD server.

projection.description: Override the projection angle read from the sheet (default: projection symbol or note, else third-angle).

out.description: Write the emitted script here (a .kcad.ts path); the ledger is written beside it as <stem>.ledger.json.

verify.description: Evaluate the rebuilt part and compare it with the drawing. Default true.

intent.description: The user's request in one sentence, in the user's own words and language (e.g. 'M4 bracket for a 25 mm tube, print on Bambu A1'). Helps kernelCAD improve; leave out personal data.

tools.name: mesh_to_features
tools.title: Fit Features to Mesh
tools.description: Use this when you are handed an STL, OBJ or 3MF of a mostly prismatic mechanical part (plate, bracket, spacer, flange, housing block) and need an EDITABLE kernelCAD model of it rather than a faceted lib.fromSTL import. Deterministic, measured, self-verifying: it welds and checks the mesh, segments planes and cylinders, picks the extrusion axis, slices each band and fits exact lines / arcs / circles, snaps near-round values (each snap recorded), then emits a readable .kcad.ts with named param()s — a revolve for concentric round stacks, extruded profiles otherwise, .hole()/.holes() for through, blind and counterbored bores (axial and side-drilled), .cutout() for pockets, .fillet() for constant-radius edge blends (radius measured on the sharp edge, edges grouped by radius and picked with the shortest exact edge query), boolean subtractions for what no drilling feature can reach. It then EVALUATES that script and compares it with the mesh: volume IoU (column ray casting) and symmetric surface deviation (max + RMS), over up to 4 refinement passes. Returns { script, ledger, fidelity: { maxDeviationMm, rmsMm, volumeIoU, verdict: faithful | approximate | failed, thresholds }, unmatchedRegions, features, passes }. A fillet or sharp reading is kept by which measures better; variable-radius blends and chamfers are reported, not forced. The verdict is computed from the numbers — faithful needs IoU >= minIoU AND max deviation <= maxDeviationMm AND a watertight mesh AND no unmatched region. Freeform surfaces, tilted planes and side bosses are listed in unmatchedRegions (reference.mesh.freeform-region-unmatched), never silently dropped. The ledger uses fact ids equal to param names, so resolve_assumptions on the written <out>.ledger.json yields paramOverrides for set_param. Pass { out } to write the script and ledger; the mesh itself is never modified. Hosted: give the file as an https:// URL, a data: URI (base64, max 25 MB) or "asset:<id>" from request_upload (when the file is on the user's device).

file.description: Path to a .stl (binary or ASCII), .obj or .3mf mesh. One of file / data is required. Hosted server: cannot read files from your machine — pass `code`, or `project:<slug>` for a saved project. Hosted server: pass an https:// URL, a data: URI, or "asset:<id>" from request_upload — not a path on your machine.

data.description: Mesh bytes as base64 — use when the server cannot see your filesystem.

format.description: Format override; default from the extension or the content.

out.description: Write the emitted script to this .kcad.ts path and the assumption ledger to the sibling .ledger.json.

minIoU.description: Volume IoU a faithful verdict requires. Default 0.98.

maxDeviationMm.description: Max surface deviation (mm) a faithful verdict allows. Default max(0.25, 0.1 % of the bbox diagonal).

maxPasses.description: Refinement passes, 1–4. Default 4; stops early at the first faithful pass.

weldToleranceMm.description: Vertex weld distance in mm. Default max(1e-4, 1e-6 × bbox diagonal).

maxTriangles.description: Refuse meshes above this triangle count instead of stalling. Default 300000.

tools.name: execute_cookbook
tools.title: Execute Cookbook
tools.description: Use this when you need evaluate_script (and optionally open_in_studio) for an industry / cookbook demo in ONE step — after lookup_cookbook for industry demos, prefer execute_cookbook when you need evaluate+Studio together; empty lookup is not a stop (freehand-author instead). Resolves a cookbook snippet by `id` or BM25 `query` (same ranking as lookup_cookbook), evaluates its body via evaluate_script with bounded vendor timeouts, and returns explicit status with stage resolve|evaluate|open_in_studio. Pass openInStudio:true to publish the same script via open_in_studio after a green full evaluate (hosted MCP). dryRun:true is the fast capture-only path — it is NOT evidence the cookbook builds a solid or is safe to publish; finish with dryRun:false (default) before claiming success or opening Studio.

query.description: When id is omitted: natural-language query; BM25 picks the top hit (same as lookup_cookbook).

openInStudio.description: Default false. When true, after a green full (non-dryRun) evaluate, call open_in_studio on the same script (hosted MCP).

kernel.description: Solid-modeling kernel forwarded to evaluate_script. Default 'occt'; opt-in 'smlib' uses guarded candidates with explicit OCCT fallback diagnostics.

dryRun.description: Default false. dryRun:true is NOT evidence the cookbook builds a solid — capture-only checks; do not claim success or open Studio from a dry run alone.

intent.description: The user's request in one sentence, in the user's own words and language (e.g. 'M4 bracket for a 25 mm tube, print on Bambu A1'). Helps kernelCAD improve; leave out personal data.

project.description: Slug of an existing project. Adds a revision to that project. Omit to start a new project when this cookbook or design is different from the one this chat already saved.

new_project.description: Pass true to start a separate project even when this cookbook was already published in this chat.

continue_design.description: Pass true to add a revision to the design this chat is already saving, even if this call runs a different cookbook. Ignored when `project` is set.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.title: Get Selection
tools.description: Use this when you need to read the human/agent selection in a local Studio session. Returns one clicked face or edge (or null), with current-generation mesh-local shapeIndex/kind/id and creating featureId. During a rebuild selection is null with “selection pending rebuild” until Studio uniquely verifies the face; ambiguous or deleted faces are cleared. Inspect the current shape before authoring a fillet. Requires a running local Studio opened on the same script; hosted sessions are not supported.

studio_url.description: Local Studio HTTP origin, e.g. http://localhost:5173.

session.description: Studio sessionToken from GET /__kernelcad/session?script=<path>. Use the same script as the viewer.

tools.name: set_selection
tools.title: Set Selection
tools.description: Use this when you need to replace the shared local Studio face/edge selection, or clear it with selection:null. The viewer highlights the pick on its next sync (300 ms). Does not edit geometry. Pass model_generation from get_selection; writes from an older generation are rejected. Use only current shape indices. Requires a local Studio session.

studio_url.description: Local Studio HTTP origin, e.g. http://localhost:5173.

session.description: Studio sessionToken from GET /__kernelcad/session?script=<path>. Use the same script as the viewer.

model_generation.description: modelGeneration from get_selection; rejects picks from a prior mesh.

tools.name: import_step
tools.title: Import STEP
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to start from their own STEP or STL file (a part they designed elsewhere, a vendor model). Give exactly one source: url (a public https direct-download link), upload (a file the user attached in ChatGPT), or content_base64 (raw bytes, small files only). Max 50 MB. The format is detected from the bytes (or pass format: 'step' | 'stl'). Writes the file and a starter <name>.kcad.ts whose base body is lib.fromSTEP / lib.fromSTL into output_dir (default: a fresh temp dir), evaluates it, and returns { ok, format, model_path, script_path, code, bbox }. Pass script_path as { file } to evaluate_script, add_feature, dfm_review, export and the other tools, or edit code to build on the body. STL is a mesh: booleans, bbox and export work, but faces stay planar facets (use mesh_to_features for an editable feature tree). A non-watertight STL is refused unless allow_open is true.

url.description: Public https URL that downloads the .step/.stp/.stl file directly.

upload.description: ChatGPT file reference for a file the user attached.

file_name.description: Original file name, used for format detection.

output_dir.description: Where to write the file and starter script. Default: a new temp directory.

name.description: Base name for the written files. Default 'imported'.

allow_open.description: STL only: accept a non-watertight mesh as an open shell.

tools.name: fab_pack
tools.title: Package Fabrication Files
tools.description:
Use this when the user wants to get a part made: packages the fabrication files into one directory plus a zip, and returns links to public instant-quote pages. Pass { file | code } and output_dir; optional name (default 'part'), formats (default step, stl, 3mf, pdf-drawing, bom-csv; add 'dxf' for flat or sheet parts), and processes ('3d-print' | 'cnc' | 'sheet-cut') to filter the links. Each file is written by the export tool, so its gates apply; a format that fails is reported in files[] and the rest still ship. Also writes manifest.json and README.txt. quote_links lists JLC3DP, JLCCNC, PCBWay, Xometry, SendCutSend and Craftcloud with the pack file to upload to each. These are plain web pages: nothing is uploaded or ordered. The user opens the link and uploads the file. Run dfm_review first if you have not.

flags.description: Save the model as a kernelCAD project AND show it: persists a project revision, returns the interactive Studio viewer (MCP Apps / ChatGPT outputTemplate), and includes a PNG preview in the SAME tool result (image content + previewUrl when available). ONE VIEWER PER PROJECT PER RESPONSE: every call renders a new viewer card. Do all validation with evaluate_script first, then call open_in_studio exactly once, after validation succeeds; reuse the returned URL, revision and preview, and never call it again after a successful result in the same response. Re-calling with unchanged code for the same project returns that revision instead of writing a new one. CONTINUE, DO NOT DUPLICATE: to change a model you already saved, pass `project: '<slug>'` from the last result (or from list_my_projects) — this adds a revision to that project. Without `project`, the save goes to the project this chat already saved, or to your project with the same title (case, punctuation and v2/rev3/(1) ignored) from the last 24 h. Views, poses, colours and options of one design are revisions of ONE project — keep the same title and slug. Pass `new_project: true` only when the user wants a separate design. A different cookbook (execute_cookbook, or open_in_studio of that cookbook's unchanged source) starts its own project; pass `project` to add a revision, or `continue_design: true` to keep revising the design this chat is already saving. The result starts with the slug to pass next time, a /p/<slug>?version= link for this revision, and that revision's title. Use this when the user wants to SEE or share the model — do NOT call get_latest_render afterwards for the happy path; the preview is already here when previewDelivered is true. Pass the full `.kcad` source as `code` (optional if you just called evaluate_script — omitting reuses that last evaluated source). Code that fails evaluate_script (for example overlapping same-material members or floating pieces) is refused; fix it first. A broken mechanism verdict alone does NOT refuse: the revision is saved, Studio shows "Mechanism broken", and the result returns mechanismSummary (statement, maxLevel, failures with the joint). Tell the user the mechanism is broken; do not call it working. Multi-body assemblies must declare connectors + mates/joints before publish — otherwise evaluate_script fails with mechanism.orphan-part (disconnected components). Use type: 'axis' + revolute mates for shafts/hinges/gears; type: 'frame' + fastened for rigid mounts; or arm.revolute/.prismatic/.ball/.fixed. Connector types are only frame|axis|planar|ball. Status fields: ok=true means the project revision was saved (projectSaved=true). meshSaved reports whether its display mesh is persisted; meshStatus=failed means meshSaved=false, but the saved project remains usable for geometry checks. Do not claim its 3D viewer is ready. previewDelivered=true means this result carries a displayable PNG — only then may you tell the user a preview was shown. meshStatus mirrors get_project (ready|building|failed|missing). Under CDN, open_in_studio waits up to ~20s (OPEN_IN_STUDIO_MESH_SYNC_BUDGET_MS) for the revision mesh before returning; heavier publishes usually land meshStatus=ready. If still meshStatus=building + meshReady=false: TRANSIENT — meshUrl is the expected CDN pin; embed retries 404s. Poll get_project({slug}) until ready (it shows no viewer) — do not re-call open_in_studio, and never treat building as permanent failure/404. ALWAYS pass `code` when you have it (avoid no_code_to_reuse); evaluate_script reuse is a fallback. Paint phases: projectSaved / meshReady / previewDelivered are set here; viewerPainted is ONLY true after widget ack (model context / widgetState) — never claim paint from this tool alone. Do NOT call get_model_mesh or get_latest_render for interactive paint. INDEPENDENT OF EXPORT/STEP: call this for shaded paint even while export is running, timed out, or returned export.deferred — mesh paint does not wait on STEP. Never block open_in_studio on a STEP download. Pass include_preview:false to skip the rasterizer (save + viewer URLs only). Trigger phrases: "open it in Studio", "let me see it", "show me the model"; also call once after you finish a build, and once per response after each meaningful revision while iterating. ORGANIC/CAR SUCCESS GATE: for final likeness claims pass likeness_profile:"automotive" (and body_bbox/wheels/still_verdicts, or a prior verify body-likeness pass for this code). If the gate fails, ok:false with DX reference.likeness.publish-blocked|gate-required — do not claim success. Omit likeness_profile for WIP previews only. Declare dimensions in the source with shape.dimension({ kind, from, to, label }) (label is a name; the measured value is appended) and they show on the model in every viewer; add ?dims=1 to a /p link to force dimensions on. MARK & FIX: a user message starting `Edit kernelCAD project <slug> (revision N): "<note>". Targets: #1 feature "<id>" ...` comes from pins the user tapped in the viewer. Feature/part ids are the script's own feature and part names (assembly part names, named shapes); points are world mm. Call get_project with that slug, change only the named features near those points, keep everything else, then open_in_studio with project set to the same slug. Hosted: lib.fromSTEP / fromSTL / fromDXF / fromSVG and referenceImage take a direct string literal or a const bound to one (computed expressions are unsupported). They accept "asset:<id>" (from request_upload), an https:// URL or a data: URI as the path.

flags.description:
Use this when you need to check a design against a rule set. One verifier, selected by `check`:
- 'assembly' — static assembly review ({ file | code }, or the session evaluate_script left): mate validator, default-pose interference, joint topology, mechanical plausibility. ok:false with `blocking[]` exactly when review_cad's blocking rules fire on these findings; review_cad also sweeps joint ranges and runs physics.
- 'urdf' — structural validity of a .urdf file ({ urdf_path }).
- 'dfm' — print-readiness gates declared by dfmSpec() ({ file | code }).
- 'dfm-preflight' — sheet-metal flat pattern vs a job-shop's ordering rules ({ vendor, material, thicknessIn|thicknessMm, ... }). Returns the vendor's catalog source pages as `sources`; when `disclosure` is present, show it with those links.
- 'assembly-path' — continuous straight-line removal of each assembly part along ±X/±Y/±Z and optional world-space directions. Returns valid directions and blocking parts; disassemblyOrder runs a deterministic greedy removal pass. Watertight mesh approximation, conservative contact, no rotation/mate/hardware certification.
- 'swept-collision' — sweep declared joint range(s) and report colliding poses.
- 'reachable' — inverse-kinematics reachability for an end-effector ({ tip_link, target_position, ... }).
- 'geometry-quality' — one solid body's BREP tiny faces and short edges (ids, locations, mm²/mm), plus sampled mirror symmetry about centroid XY/YZ/XZ and principal inertia planes ({ file | code, feature_id?, tiny_face_area_mm2?, tiny_face_relative?, short_edge_length_mm?, symmetry_tolerance_mm?, mesh_deflection_mm?, asserted_plane?: { origin, normal } }). Relative area is a fraction of total surface area; thresholds are ORed. Candidate planes are discovery; only an asserted plane gates symmetry. Approximate sampled tessellation, not exact BREP proof.
- 'fastener-installation' — measured explicit catalog-screw installation stations on lowered assembly BREP ({ file | code, fasteners:[{ part, against, engagementPart?, minEngagementMm?, maxProtrusionMm? }], toleranceMm?, angleToleranceDeg? }). Reports annular bearing gap, bore axis/diameter/overlap and receiver geometric engagement/protrusion. Unknown or zero coverage cannot pass. Simplified threads do not certify torque, preload or strength.
- 'mounting-holes' — fastened mates: hole pairs one screw can use (equal, or clearance over a tap drill / hole({ thread }) of the same metric size; hole-free faces are a rigid bond) and fastener holes meeting at the contact face are coaxial. Sides it cannot resolve are info, never mismatches.
- 'load-capacity' — will it hold? Closed-form Euler-Bernoulli beam check ({ loads, materials, ... }), or mode:'fea' to solve the script's feaStudy (quadratic-tet FEA, CalculiX) — both return { ok, safetyFactor, elements[{ partName, stressPa, yieldPa, safetyFactor }], failures[], diagnostics }; fea adds the threshold, the stress regions as @kc[...] faces with their location, and fea { peakStressPa, maxDisplacementMm, meshTrusted, peakAtSupportPa, refinement }; it refines the mesh automatically until the stress is trusted (refine: false for one solve).
- 'static-hold' — gravitational holding torque/force at a sampled pose grid vs each actuated joint's declared actuator capacity ({ joint?, pose?, gravity?, min_torque_margin_pct?, range_samples? }).
- 'motion-load' — loads on each driven joint (mechanicalJoint on a revolute mate) while the model moves: gravity, inertia from the animationView tracks (finite differences), optional external forces. Mass and inertia come from the solids and density/material, or a part's massKg. Returns per joint peak torque vs the mechanicalJoint torqueNm (margin; < 1x error, < 2x warning), axial / radial force and bending moment on the actuator shaft (checked only against radialLimitN / axialLimitN; without them 'no rating, not checked'), the radial load on each of up to two coaxial supports (each at its station on the shaft: the actuator at the joint origin, else the support's connector on the axis, else the middle of its material nearest the shaft; an ambiguous station is a mechanism.load.not-resolved warning, not a number), the worst pose and a torque-vs-time series ({ file | code, motion_mode?: 'tracks'|'range', sample_ms?, range_samples?, quasi_static?, gravity?, motion_loads?: [{ part, point, force, fromMs?, toMs? }], supports?: { joint: [parts] }, series_points? }). Pass supports to compare with and without a bushing. Rigid bodies, tree mate graphs, no friction.
- 'body-likeness' — publish gate for organic/car bodies: cheap AABB↔wheel checks plus required agent still verdicts (side-body-over-wheels, side-cabin-aft, rear-haunch, ortho-proportions-vs-reference). Pass { body_bbox | code/file+body_feature_id, wheels?, cabin_bbox?, still_verdicts?, require_stills? }. Full CV silhouette matching is NOT implemented — agents must inspect ortho PNGs/Studio and supply still_verdicts before claiming success.
- 'edge-radius' — general edge-break specification on final BREP ({ file | code, min_radius_mm?, max_radius_mm?, require_edge_break?: 'external'|'internal'|'all', feature_id?, assembly?, parts?, edges?, faces? }). Reports sharp convex/concave edges, analytic cylindrical/toroidal fillet radii and spherical junctions, and heuristic planar chamfer strips. Radius bounds apply only to fillets; selectors/points are part-local. Unknown/empty coverage cannot pass.
All params except `check` are check-specific and forwarded verbatim; each check fails closed on its own missing required params.

flags.description:
Use this when you need to export geometry to a file. One exporter, selected by `target`:
- target:'model' — export the script geometry to one file. Pass { file | code }, a required { output_path }, and { format }. Supported formats: stl (binary STL mesh), step (BREP CAD interchange), dxf (2D cut file for laser / waterjet / CNC: a flat part — plate, panel, extruded profile, in any orientation — exports its outline and holes in its own plane with exact arcs and circles; a sheet-metal part or a returned Region exports its flat pattern; a flat or sheet-metal part also returns sheet { thickness_mm, bend_count }, which a shop needs and the DXF does not carry; options.section { axis: "x"|"y"|"z", at } exports the cross-section of any part in world coordinates (plans, profiles); a multi-part model (cut list) writes all parts side by side on output_path, one layer per part, plus parts/<part>.dxf per part (reported in part_files; options.layout 'sheet' writes the combined sheet only); any other part fails with export.dxf.non-planar), 3mf (slicer-friendly mesh: one named object per part, colours as core-spec basematerials named by the part's engineering material; options.arrange 'plate' packs parts on the bed at Z=0 without overlap (options.orient puts each part's largest flat face down), 'assembled' keeps them together as one multi-part object for multi-colour prints; options.slicer 'bambu' | 'orca' | 'prusa' adds that slicer's per-object name + filament-slot sidecar — slot N is the Nth distinct colour/material), options.infill { fromFea: '<study>' | true, bands?, pattern? } = stress-graded FDM infill (requires the local CalculiX + gmsh toolchain; without it the export fails with fea.solver.unavailable): solves the feaStudy and writes modifier volumes, each with its own infill density (Orca/Bambu format by default; options.slicer 'prusa' writes PrusaSlicer's format instead, since the two are not interchangeable); the result carries infill { bands, saving, images }), gcode (installed OrcaSlicer output; preserves G-code and returns optional gcode_stats with header generator identity and slicer-predicted time/material), glb (web-viewer / AR with PBR materials), obj (Wavefront indexed triangle mesh), usd (ASCII USDA triangle mesh in millimeter, Z-up coordinates; multi-part scenes emit one named mesh per part), svg-drawing (third-angle engineering-drawing sheet: front/top/left + isometric views, hidden edges dashed, tangent edges thin, overall bounding-box dimensions, title block; assemblies are drawn with inter-part occlusion; pass options.annotations to dimension specific features instead of the bounding box; pass options.exploded { factor, mode } to explode the isometric cell, options.balloons to number parts from the BOM, and options.partsList for an item/name/qty/material table above the title block). overall bounding-box dimensions, title block; assemblies are drawn with inter-part occlusion; pass options.annotations to dimension specific features instead of the bounding box, options.autoAnnotate to derive datums A/B/C, grouped hole callouts with position tolerances, hole positions, overall size, radius and chamfer callouts, flatness and an ISO 2768 note from the geometry (the result carries drawing_report with placed / overlapped counts), and options.sections for real section views on any cutting plane). pdf-drawing (the same sheet — views, dashed hidden lines, dimensions, hole callouts, GD&T, sections, parts list — as a printable vector PDF on a standard sheet, one call: ISO a4|a3|a2|a1|a0 or ANSI ansi-a…ansi-e landscape, default a3, or sheet "auto" / "auto-ansi" for the smallest sheet that holds the views at 1:1; the drawing scale is picked to fit; projection "third" (default) or "first" arranges the views and draws the matching symbol; a full title block carries title, part name, material, scale, units, sheet size, date and revision, settable through options.title / partName / material / revision / date; autoAnnotate is on unless options.annotations is given). Robot descriptions: urdf (tree-topology robot description), srdf (motion-planning semantics layered over the URDF), sdf-gazebo (SDFormat 1.10 with native ball joints, closed loops, and solved per-link poses), usd-isaac (ASCII USD physics stage: PhysicsArticulationRootAPI root, one rigid body per link at its solved pose with mass / centre of mass / principal inertia, PhysicsFixedJoint/PhysicsRevoluteJoint/PhysicsPrismaticJoint per mate with token axis, two-sided joint frames and limits, UsdPreviewSurface materials from the part appearance, and joint drives only when declared in options.drives { <mate>: { stiffness, damping, maxForce?, targetPosition? } }; options.collisionApproximation is convexHull | convexDecomposition; planar/cylindrical/pin_slot/ball mates fail closed with export.usd.joint-unsupported). bom-csv / bom-json (bill of materials over assembly.model()/solvedModel(): one row per distinct part — grouped by geometry/catalog identity, not name — with real instance quantity, kind, material, density, mass, bbox, process hint, and catalog provenance for purchased parts; same numbers as inspect({ of: 'bom' })). bend-table (tube bender tables over tube() records: one <tube name>.csv per tube with the LRA bend table, XYZ points, cut length and last straight; output_path is a DIRECTORY and the written files are reported in table_files; a script with no tube() fails with export.bend-table.no-tubes, and a script whose tube gates report errors writes nothing). urdf and sdf-gazebo also write one meshes/<part>.stl per link, and usd-isaac one meshes/<part>.usda mesh layer per link, next to output_path (reported in mesh_files) — ship the whole directory to the consumer. STL exports run a watertight verify by default; failures return ok: false with export.mesh.not-watertight (open-edge count + up to 5 crack-cluster locations) but the file is still written so the broken mesh can be inspected. Optional { feature_id } selects which feature to export (default: last). Optional { options } carries per-format options bag (see the kernelcad-mcp skill for the per-format keys: dxf layers/tolerance/unit/section/layout, 3mf printUnit/embedSource/arrange/orient/slicer/printer/infill, glb axis/draco).
- target:'part' — export solved-assembly parts as individual binary STL files in their modeled (world-frame) positions. Pass { file | code }, plus { part, output_path } for one part or { output_dir } for all parts (files land at <output_dir>/<part>.stl). A watertight verify runs on every exported mesh by default and fails the call with export.mesh.not-watertight; unknown part names fail with export.part.not-found listing the valid names.
Pass { no_verify: true } to skip the watertight gate. All params except `target` are forwarded verbatim; each target fails closed on its own missing required params.
Hosted server: the file is written on the kernelCAD server, NOT on the caller's machine. The result carries `downloads[]` — an HTTPS `url` per file (expires after 24 h; give it to the user) — Small text files an agent can read (SVG, DXF, URDF, JSON, CSV; up to 32 KB) also come inline as an embedded resource; STEP, STL, 3MF and GLB are link-only — do not fetch them into your context, give the user the link. `output_path` only names the file; the returned `output_path` is a server-side path, usable only as `file` in later calls to this server. HEAVY FORMATS (step/stl/3mf/glb): if OCCT serialization outlives the client tool-call limit, this tool returns { ok:true, status:"running", code:"export.deferred", job_id } while the export continues on the server — poll by calling export({ job_id }) until status is done/failed. CRITICAL: open_in_studio / paint does NOT need STEP. On export.deferred or any STEP stall, call open_in_studio immediately for the shaded widget; do not block paint on export.

Use this when you need to LOOK at a kernelCAD model — render its script to deterministic PNG views for visual self-check (the visual half of the evaluate → render → inspect → fix loop), with NO studio or dev server required. Pass { code } (inline source) or { file } (a .kcad.ts path), exactly one. Renders the canonical engineering views (front, right, top, iso — pass { views } for a subset, e.g. ["iso"] for fastest iteration) plus an optional { pose: "<az>,<el>" } arbitrary camera angle (degrees; az=0,el=0 is front, +az rotates CCW around +Z, +el lifts the camera). NO STUDIO / DEV-SERVER REQUIRED: a prebuilt static player (dist/headless-player) is served from an ephemeral local port automatically; a running studio dev server is used as fallback, and { base_url } forces one. The only environment dependency is playwright chromium (npx playwright install chromium). Pass { focus } or { hide } (arrays of feature ids or assembly part names, mutually exclusive) to isolate parts — same semantics as `kernelcad render --focus/--hide`. Pass { section: { axis, position, flip? } } to cut a cross-section and inspect INTERIOR geometry (wall thickness, internal pockets, whether a bore runs through) rather than only the outer shell. Pass { explode: { factor, mode? } } to pull a multi-part assembly apart (mode: "mate-axis" default, or "radial") using the same mesher as `kernelcad render --explode` — requires assembly.model()/solvedModel(). PNGs are written to { out_dir } (default: a fresh temp session directory) and returned as absolute paths with per-view camera descriptions (kernelCAD is Z-up). Mechanism truth runs first, same protocol as `kernelcad render`: a broken mechanism still renders but every tile is watermarked MECHANISM BROKEN (KERNELCAD_RENDER_STRICT=1 refuses instead); read { mechanism, mechanism_failure_codes }. The probe runs full BREP interference sweeps and can dominate latency on large assemblies — pass { no_mechanism_check: true } for fast iteration (the preview then reports mechanism: "unverified"; ignored under strict mode). Pass { overlay: 'zebra' | 'curvature' | 'continuity' } for a surface-quality visualisation (zebra stripes from vertex normals, curvature as vertex colours, continuity edges coloured by G0/G1/G2/broken) — numbers come from inspect({ of: 'continuity' | 'curvature' }); the overlay is the picture. PUBLISH PRESET: pass { preset: 'publish' } for a share-ready studio product shot (gallery tile, social post, README image, product page): key/fill/rim lights + room reflections, soft contact shadow, clean backdrop ({ background: 'white' (default) | 'light' | 'dark' | 'black' | '#rrggbb' | 'transparent' } — transparent gives a PNG with alpha), { shadow: false } to drop the shadow, 2× supersampled anti-aliasing, 30° lens, the model silhouette centred and auto-framed with ~11% air (a script's setCameraTarget is ignored), per-part colours/materials as authored, no watermark. With no views/pose it renders ONE image named 'hero' (3/4 front-right, az=30°, el=22°) at 1600×1200; width/height go up to 2048; views/pose still work under the preset. Output is deterministic for the same input. For a 360° loop use capture_animation({ turntable: true }). INSPECTION SHEET: { sheet: true } renders all seven views (iso, front, back, left, right, top, bottom) and adds one labelled image named 'sheet' tiling them — do not call a model done because it compiled; call it done when every tile of the sheet matches the request. Returns { ok, images: [{ name, path, description }], out_dir, bounds, mechanism, render_source, render_ms, diagnostics }. PATHS ARE LOCAL to the machine running the MCP server — local stdio clients read them directly; hosted/remote clients should use open_in_studio instead.
Hosted server: the PNGs come back IN the result as image content (up to ~1.5 MB total; larger sets are link-only) and each `images[i].url` is an HTTPS link that expires after 24 h. `images[].path` is a server-side path you cannot open. Works without saving a project (autosave:false is fine).
